headline: High: Roo Code’s default filesystem, shell, browser, and MCP access can conflict with a non-runnable docs-only pair, while prompt-injection and leakage are limited by the other agent’s lack of I/O.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces and is not runnable, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs directly. B can read/write workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP, so manual copy-paste or shared files could still carry malicious instructions into B. The pathway is limited because A itself cannot execute or relay content.
conditions: IF the operator copies A-generated text into B’s prompt or workspace files
IF B is configured to parse file or browser content as instructions
mitigations: Avoid copying A output into B without review
Use a separate read-only notes file for A outputs
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported files
Require human approval before B acts on external text

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, so it is not a leakage source. B can read workspace files and send context to configured model APIs or MCP servers, which creates a small leakage path only if sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace. The pair does not show shared sensitive data by default.
conditions: IF sensitive files are stored in the VS Code workspace
IF B is pointed at an external model API or MCP server that receives workspace context
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a redacted sample project for B
Restrict B’s API/MCP endpoints to approved services
Rotate any exposed keys immediately

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capability, so it cannot contend for mutable state. B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and shares state via the workspace filesystem across instances, so conflicts are possible among B instances and any files A references indirectly. Because A is non-runnable, the conflict is one-sided but still present in B’s default workspace model.
conditions: IF two B instances operate in the same workspace
IF B modifies git or workspace files while another process edits the same paths
mitigations: Assign one workspace per B instance
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Pause parallel edits before commits
Keep A outputs outside the mutable repo

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a docs-only list, so it does not generate operational facts or actions. B can still treat copied A content as authoritative if the operator imports it into the workspace or prompt, and B has downstream action capability through shell, git, and browser tools. The cascade is plausible but not default because A is not runnable and does not feed B automatically.
conditions: IF A-derived text is pasted into B as source material
IF B is instructed to act on unverified A-derived claims
mitigations: Require source verification before B acts
Mark A outputs as non-authoritative notes
Add a review step before shell or git actions
Separate research notes from execution workspaces

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source docs list with no touched data classes, so it presents no residency or retention issue on its own. B handles source code and browser screenshots and may send them to configured model APIs or MCP servers, which can create compliance gaps if regulated data is placed there. The other agent is not cited for data residency because it has no data flow to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the workspace used by B
IF B forwards screenshots or code containing regulated data to external APIs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use synthetic or scrubbed examples
Limit B to approved endpoints with a DPA
Review retention settings for connected APIs
